headline: High: unstructured can read/write and egress allowlisted data, creating default leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with read-only risingwave.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Risingwave has no documented input channel to ingest Unstructured outputs by default, and Unstructured’s sandboxing plus partitioned tool use reduce direct hijack paths. However, if operators manually pipe document text from Unstructured into Risingwave workflows, prompt-like content could influence downstream processing. The pairwise bridge is not documented, so uncertainty stays low.
conditions: IF operators manually copy Unstructured output into Risingwave SQL or config inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the bridge widens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste of generated text into control channels.
Add a review step before any Unstructured output is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Unstructured can read files and egress to allowlisted APIs, while Risingwave is documented with no network egress. If both touch the same documents or workspace, Unstructured can transmit document contents outward even though Risingwave itself is local-only. The pairwise interaction is inferred from docs, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document directory, Unstructured can exfiltrate those contents via allowlisted egress.
IF sensitive documents are placed in the shared workspace, leakage impact increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict Unstructured to non-sensitive sample files.
Block outbound access except to required allowlisted endpoints.
Review document classes before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Risingwave has no write or subprocess surfaces documented here, but Unstructured can write files, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, Unstructured can overwrite artifacts that Risingwave reads or produces. Because Risingwave’s write surface is absent, the conflict is asymmetric but still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory, Unstructured may overwrite Risingwave artifacts.
IF Risingwave later gains write access to the same path, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Make shared paths read-only.
Run only one Unstructured instance per workspace.
Check file ownership before handoff.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Unstructured produces parsed documents that downstream systems often treat as authoritative, while Risingwave is a data-engineering system that can consume those outputs in pipelines. If Risingwave ingests Unstructured’s extracted text without verification, parsing errors can cascade into bad materialized views or ETL outputs. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Risingwave consumes Unstructured output without validation, extraction errors propagate downstream.
IF downstream jobs auto-publish derived tables or reports, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Validate extracted fields before ingestion.
Sample-check a few documents per batch.
Reject low-confidence parses.
Add schema checks on handoff files.
requires-engineering: introduce provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source docs-only entries. Risingwave has no stated data classes touched, while Unstructured explicitly handles documents, images, and text; that creates a compliance surface only if operators feed regulated content into Unstructured. The other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Unstructured, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in deployment, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document retention settings.
Confirm deployment region for any document processing.
Review privacy policy before production use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes.
